# Slime People
Comprised of slime, this humanoid species breathes nitrogen instead of oxygen. Which, while it is abundant in the station air, it is harder to find compressed into gas tanks. They exhale nitrous oxide and are unaffected by it.
## Background
Your kind were (and often are still) considered one of the many pests of the galaxy.
Fleeting, amorphous, and nearly impossible to contain, you were seen as little more than a nuisance or something to experiment on. Your kind were an unpredictable hazard on ships and in colonies alike. Few paused to consider the intelligence behind your shifting forms, or the adaptability that allowed you to thrive in environments others could not.
Able to survive almost anywhere, your kind often infested stations, both by accident and design. Most saw you as hostile; others merely as a curiosity. It wasn’t until humans began observing and studying you that they realized you were far more intelligent and diverse than anyone had imagined. Your capacity for learning, mimicry, and problem-solving challenged the very notion of what a “species” could be.
Decades later, the so-called “slime people” chose a new path. Many of you stayed within human civilization rather than return to a purely primal existence. You learned to take on humanoid forms to better navigate this new world, occasionally incorporating borrowed materials like bones, shells, or other structures to maintain a recognizable shape. This choice allowed you to blend, communicate, and even participate in human society while preserving the essence of your fluid nature. Now your evolution has given you bigger goals than just survival: it gave you an identity.
## Unique Abilities
### Membrane Storage
- Slimepeople have an [bold]internal 2x3 storage inventory[/bold] inside of their slime membrane. - Anyone can see what's inside and take it out of you without asking, so be careful.
## Diet - Slime Blood is technically a source of moderately filling food for other species, although drinking the blood of your coworkers is usually frowned upon.
## Benefits
- They [color=#1e90ff]suffocate 80% slower.[/color] This makes them by far the species most capable to survive in hard vacuum. For a while. - They take [color=#1e90ff]40% less Blunt damage and 20% less Poison damage[/color] - Slimepeople have [color=#1e90ff]accelerated regeneration[/color] compared to other humanoids. - Slimepeople have [color=#1e90ff]no bones to break.[/color]
## Drawbacks
- They take [color=#ffa500]significant damage if they are sprayed or splashed with water[/color], but can (and like other species, need to) drink it safely to stay hydrated. - They take [color=#ffa500]50% more Cold damage, 15% more Slash damage and 15% more Piercing damage[/color]. - As a result of their lack of bones, [color=#ffa500]their limbs come off easier.[/color] - Their body [color=#ffa500]processes only two toxins at a time[/color] compared to three. - They take [color=#ffa500]pressure damage 9% faster.[/color]
